rows.en:
(Even if they say they found a new planet,
I can't really picture it...)
rows.notes: Male, nml_nns_003. "atarashii hoshi" = the newly found planet.

rows.en: \p-kun, what's up?
rows.notes: Nanase (male variant), also in nml_nns_011 where the player is lost in thought; fits both.

rows.en: Oh, I was just thinking about the new planet...
Oh, really? Is there something about it?

No, it's the opposite.
I just can't picture it at all.
That's true. I have no idea what it'll be like either.
Right...?

But with Ranka-san and everyone at Mihoshi...
no, with everyone on the Frontier,
I'm sure we'll be fine!
Yeah, you're right!
(No point worrying about what I can't know.)

(Even if they say they found a new planet...
I just can't picture it...)
\p-san, what's up?
Nothing, I was just thinking about the new planet...

No, it's the opposite.
I just can't imagine it at all.
Yeah, I'm sure you're right!
(No sense worrying about what I can't know.)

(Whoa, I spaced out at school,
and now look how late it is...)
Huh? \p-kun?
rows.notes: Nanase (male variant); also Ranka in nml_rnk_024 male. Fits both.

rows.en: Nanase? What are you doing out this late?

Well, I was at my part-time job,
and before I knew it, it was this late...
What, you worked this late? That's rough...

No, it's not that. After work,
I got to talking with Ranka-san, and...
Oh, I see. That explains it...
Oh! I have to hurry home. Bye for now!
Get home safe!

(I wonder what Nanase was talking about
until this late...)

(Whoa, I spaced out at school,
and now it's this late...)
Huh? \p-san?
Huh, Nanase? What are you doing out this late?
What, you worked this late? That's rough...
Oh, I see. That explains it...
Be careful on your way home!

(I wonder what Nanase was talking about
until this late...)
(The city... the Frontier is in ruins...)
\p-kun, you're safe!
rows.notes: Nanase (male variant). The row also has PLAYER occurrences near the end of both variants (after the last spoken line, before the closing monologue); they look like a duplicate string in the script. Translated as Nanase's line.

rows.en: You're safe too, Nanase.
Yes, but... the city...
Yeah. I never thought it would get this bad...
This... isn't a dream... is it...?
Yeah... I really wish it were just a dream...

(I have to stop the damage from
getting any worse...)
rows.notes: Both variants, the player (a pilot) resolving to protect the city; subject "I" restored.

rows.en: (The city... the Frontier is in ruins...)
\p-san, you're safe!
You're safe too, Nanase.
Yeah... I never thought it would get this bad...
Yeah... I really wish it were just a dream...
(The tests are finally over~...)
Good work, \p-kun.
rows.notes: Male. Nanase (otsukaresama desu), after the tests.

rows.en: Oh, Nanase. How'd the tests go?

Let's see...
I think I did about as well as usual.
You always get good grades, Nanase.
Oh, well...
rows.notes: Nanase (both variants); also the female player in nml_she_014. Neutral enough for both.

rows.en:
You've got your part-time job, and you still
do all your Art Course assignments...
You're seriously amazing, Nanase.

Geez! Flattering me like that
won't get you anything!
(Seriously, does Nanase even have any flaws...?)
Good work, \p-san.
You always do get good grades, Nanase.

(Honestly, I wonder if Nanase has
any flaws at all...)

(It's this late already?
I've got to hurry to the next classroom!)
Ah, sorry, Nanase!
rows.notes: Male; the player bumped into her.

rows.en:
No, I was in a bit of a hurry too...
I'm sorry.
Can you stand? You're not hurt or anything?
Yeah, I'm fine. Thanks.
rows.notes: Nanase (both variants); also Akimizu in nml_yuu_008. Fits both.

rows.en: Good. I'm glad you're okay...

\p-kun,
you're so kind...

Huh? Oh, I wouldn't say that...
Oh, right, we have to hurry!
rows.notes: Both variants; both are late, so "we".

rows.en: That's right, let's hurry!
(Phew, glad nothing bad happened~)

(It's this late already?
I need to hurry to the next classroom!)
Ah, I'm sorry, Nanase!

\p-san,
you're so kind...

(Nanase's eyes looked kind of...
Maybe it's just my imagination...)
rows.notes: Female. Hint at Nanase's gaze; kept vague as in the Japanese.

uncertain: c18630: also listed as PLAYER lines at the end of both variants of nml_nns_005 (a male-only '-kun' string in the female branch too), most likely a duplicate/unused string; translated as Nanase's line.
c18636: subject restored as 'I' (the pilot player resolving to stop further damage).
